{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / The Associated Press)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Exhibit 10.14 Master Services Agreement, dated 5 February  
**Status:** 19 rules assessed — 2 critical, 3 high, 11 medium, 1 low; 9 compliant, 7 deviations, 3 missing

---

## Executive summary

The Agreement is unusually clean on the restrictive-covenant side: it imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-commitment, audit or liquidated-damages obligation on us, and Section 1 expressly preserves our freedom to sell Inventory through other agents. Those positions sit at or above our preferred position and we do not intend to volunteer any of them back.

Our exposure is concentrated in three areas. First, two critical gaps: there is **no IP or data ownership provision at all**, so we take no rights in deliverables and nothing limits Kubient's use of our Content, Requests or visitor data; and **there is no aggregate liability cap anywhere**, leaving both parties' direct liability unlimited. Second, the **exit mechanics** are one-sided in effect: the Agreement auto-renews for successive one-year terms with no Customer non-renewal election, Kubient may take a mid-renewal convenience exit, and termination triggers no transition assistance or data return. Third, several **allocation-of-risk provisions** need conforming work — an assignment clause that lets Kubient transfer to a competitor without consent, a mandatory AAA arbitration clause that contradicts the exclusive-jurisdiction submission in Section 14(a), a licence grant that excludes affiliates and cannot follow us through an M&A event, a warranty set with no conformance warranty or remedy, and no vendor insurance despite Kubient hosting the platform and holding our visitor data.

We have drafted to the fallback wherever the fallback is reachable without collateral rewrites, and to preferred only where the fallback would leave us worse off (indemnity) or where the preferred language is no harder to land (governing law, insurance).

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue and our position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation (missing clause) | Preamble | No IP or data ownership provision exists. We insert the playbook fallback: Kubient keeps its generic tools and know-how (consistent with its retained platform ownership warranty), we take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables, and Kubient's licence in our data is limited to processing solely to provide the Services. Preferred-level assignment was not pursued because it would contradict the retained ownership warranty; this sits at the fallback. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | Preamble (Section 7) | Section 7 excludes consequential damages mutually but contains **no aggregate cap**; none appears in the fees, warranty, indemnity or general provisions. Direct liability is unlimited both ways, failing the fallback. We add one sentence creating a mutual 12-month fees cap with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap. The preferred USD 1,000,000 floor and additional carve-outs remain available as further asks. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Preamble (¶ 9(h)) | The no-consent affiliate/successor carve-out is mutual, so Kubient may transfer to any acquirer — including our competitor — without consent. We keep our own carve-out and the mutual reasonable-consent standard verbatim, limit the exception to Customer, bar assignment to a Customer competitor, and confirm a change of control of Customer gives Kubient no termination right. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant (preferred) | Preamble (Section 1) | Section 1 expressly negates exclusivity and preserves our right to sell Inventory through other agents. No ROFR, minimum volume or requirements commitment. No redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant (preferred) | Preamble | No liquidated damages, penalty, minimum-fee-on-termination or early-termination fee payable by us. Section 4(a) entitles Kubient only to its revenue share on fees actually generated in the notice period, and is disapplied on termination for material breach. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant (preferred) | Preamble | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us; the only Customer-side restrictions are ordinary licence-use limits on the Kubient Service. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Preamble (Sections 8 and 14(a)) | Section 14(a) picks Delaware law but a New York forum, and Section 8 mandates AAA arbitration, displacing the courts and contradicting 14(a). Both checklist levels fail. We move to preferred: New York law with the state and federal courts in New York County as exclusive merits forum, conforming Section 8 (and its heading) and leaving the jury waiver and one-year limitation untouched. |
| Medium | INDEMN — Vendor indemnification | Deviation | Preamble (Sections 10–11) | Section 10(a) already gives us a broad, uncapped Kubient indemnity with full procedure in Section 11 — materially at preferred, and we do not seek the fallback's procure/modify/replace menu or 3x super-cap, which would be worse for us. Two preferred elements fail: our affiliates are omitted from the indemnified group, and our reciprocal indemnity in 10(b) is too broad. We add affiliates and cut 10(b) back to Customer-supplied Content/Properties and our own breach of Law. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | Preamble (¶ 2) | The Auction Platform licence runs only to "Customer" (The Associated Press alone, no defined Affiliate) and is expressly non-transferable and non-assignable, failing both fallback elements. We draft at fallback: affiliate coverage on written notice and transfer to an M&A successor. Perpetual/irrevocable wording was not pursued as it would require rewriting the revocation mechanic in ¶ 4(c)(ii); the retained "revocable" wording and absence of contractor coverage are noted, not redlined. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | Preamble (¶ 4(a)) | Successive one-year renewals (length compliant) with **no Customer mechanism to stop a renewal** — the only exit is the mutual 90-day "any reason" right after the Initial Term, failing the 60-day fallback ceiling and sitting at the walk-away boundary. We carve a Customer 60-day non-renewal election into the renewal trigger, preserving the rest of 4(a) and 4(b) verbatim. No price-uplift mechanic is engaged. |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | Preamble (¶ 4(a)) | The mutual "any reason" right lets Kubient exit mid-renewal with no term-boundary anchor — a Vendor mid-term convenience exit. We split the sentence: our 90-day right stated expressly; Kubient's 90-day notice effective only at the end of the then-current Term. The early-termination-fee element is already met. The 12-month Initial Term lock-out is noted, not flagged. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Deviation (missing clause) | Preamble (Section 4(c)) | Section 4(c) only stops the Services, revokes the licence and addresses Confidential Information. No transition assistance and **no obligation to return or export our data**; the survival clause does not cure this. We insert the fallback: 90 days of transition assistance and export of our data within 30 days of expiry or termination. Preferred extras (six months at then-current rates, machine-readable format, certified deletion) are our upgrade position. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Preamble (Section 9(b), Section 13) | Section 9(b) contains a substantive warranty set preserved by the Section 13 disclaimer, so this is not an "AS IS" walk-away. But there is no documentation conformance warranty for the platform, software or deliverables, and **no warranty remedy at all**. The continuing Service warranty in 9(b)(ii) already satisfies the services duration. We add a 90-day conformance warranty with repair, replacement or refund. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant (better than preferred) | Preamble | No audit, inspection, records-examination or cost-shifting right runs against us. The cooperation covenant is delivery access, not audit; "as measured by Kubient" is a measurement convention. We will not insert audit machinery that would create exposure we do not currently have. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant (preferred) | Preamble (Section 5) | No MFN, price-matching, best-terms or right-to-match mechanic. The Winning Bid Price floor operates in our favour. No redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume | Compliant (preferred) | Preamble (Sections 1, 5, 13) | Pure revenue share on revenue actually generated; Services only as engaged under Exhibits. Section 13 confirms no minimum revenue is guaranteed; the ¶ 3(j) price floor benefits us. No shortfall or penalty mechanic. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant (preferred) | Preamble | No non-solicit, no-hire or non-inducement covenant, and the integration clause imports none. We should not volunteer a mutual non-solicit. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation (missing clause) | Preamble (General Provisions) | No insurance obligation anywhere, and no exhibit supplies one. Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and collects, stores and manages our visitor data, so an uninsured data-processing vendor sits in walk-away territory. We insert at preferred: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M where Kubient processes our data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request. Fallback available (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). |

---

## Walk-away items

Two findings reach walk-away territory on our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating positions:

1. **Auto-renewal with no Customer non-renewal right (¶ 4(a) — RENEWAL).** Indefinite one-year renewals that we cannot stop, with the only exit being a post-Initial-Term 90-day notice, sit at the walk-away boundary. Sixty days is the fallback ceiling; we should not concede a longer window.
2. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE).** Kubient hosts the platform and processes our visitor data with no insurance covenant of any kind. An uninsured data-processing vendor is walk-away territory; the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) are the floor.

We also flag, without characterising them as walk-away, that the **absence of any liability cap** and the **absence of any IP or data ownership provision** are the two commercially largest gaps in the document and should be resolved in the first exchange.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven deviations and three missing-clause inserts: IP/data ownership, mutual 12-month liability cap, assignment, governing law and venue (including conforming Section 8), licence scope, indemnity, renewal, termination for convenience, transition and data export, warranty conformance and remedy, and insurance.
2. **Sequence the negotiation** as: (a) liability cap and IP/data ownership; (b) renewal and insurance as walk-away items; (c) assignment, transition and arbitration removal; (d) licence, indemnity and warranty as conforming asks.
3. **Hold our fallbacks in reserve** — insurance at E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M; the USD 1,000,000 cap floor and additional cap carve-outs (data protection, fraud, IP, payment obligations) as second-round asks; preferred transition terms (six months at then-current rates, machine-readable export, certified deletion) as upgrades only.
4. **Do not open** the compliant items — exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum commitments, liquidated damages and audit rights. Each currently sits at or above our preferred position and reopening them invites obligations we do not have.
5. **Re-read in context** the drafting for RENEWAL (¶ 4(a) non-renewal carve) and T4C (¶ 4(a) split exit), both of which required repair during verification, to confirm the two edits to the same paragraph interlock cleanly before the redline goes out.
6. **Confirm with the business** whether any affiliate is expected to use the Auction Platform, which drives how hard we press the licence-scope and indemnity affiliate points."}
